chapter: Will Vodery and the road shows
title: Vodery's Ziegfeld scores and Bert Williams in Boston
summary: Whaley says Ziegfeld called Vodery the greatest writer, and recalls drinking with Bert Williams at an inter-racial Boston bar.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And Vodrey used to write some beautiful music.
Yeah, do you remember the thing -- he did scores for -- what show was that, it was --
Ziegfeld Follies. Man, Ziegfeld said he was the greatest musician around. Greatest writer.
He scored for Ziegfeld when Bert Williams was one of the comedians.
Oh, Bert Williams, comes to me, Bert Williams, up in Boston. I used to hang out with him on Washington and Pembroke. We used to come there, Bert Williams used to come there and I used to hang out.
Tell us about it. What kind of a guy was he? I never saw him, but I read about him.
He was -- I'm brown-skinned, Bud was a yellow man.
He was lighter in complexion than you.
Oh, yeah.
And you're a light brown skin.
Yeah, Bert Williams --
He was what we would call in our black society moriani. Is that right, would you say?
I don't know.
What would you call it?
I'd call him a yellow man.
Well, high yellow is the word we used, yes, okay.
And he would stand there at the bar and sip his beer and tell more jokes, man, he'd had everybody laughing. Bert Williams.
What bar was this in Boston?
This was up there in Washington Street, the corner of Pembroke.
Was this a black bar or was it an inter-racial bar?
No, it was an inter-racial bar.
Anybody could come in.
Sure, anybody come in.
What year was this?
Oh, let me see. This was way back in 1912, 13.
Maybe a little later, huh?
Yeah.
This was before he came to New York?
No, he used to come to Boston from New York.
After you (unintelligible) with Ziegfeld?
Playing in the show, yeah. He used to come in after he opened here and come to New York -- I mean, come to Boston. He and -- what's that other guy?
Eddie Cantor?
No.
Al Jolson?
No. Oh, I can't think of his name. Anyway, he was a great entertainer. But Bert Williams --
Harry --
No, that ain't the name. But they used to --
Bert Williams was in Ziegfeld's, too, wasn't he? He used to open the show, didn't he?
I think so.
